sections.title: Printable season summary check
sections.what: Runs one browser flow that locks four calls, opens the season summary, and checks counts, best and worst reads, charts, calibration, money-word absence, print layout and accessibility.
sections.why: Likely reason: the printed summary must be honest learning feedback without money language.
sections.watch_out: Setting the EVIDENCE variable writes a PDF into the project folder.

summary: A browser test that creates a user with four locked calls and checks the printable season summary shows the right counts, best and worst reads, charts, calibration and no money words.
purpose: Protects the season summary page: correct totals, print layout, no money language, and accessibility.
why: Likely reason: a printed summary must read as learning feedback and never as betting or payouts.
how: Creates a user and signs in. Locks four calls, two on the best option and two on the worst. Opens the season file page and checks the summary line, the best and worst lists with two items each, the reliability and rating charts, the calibration label and the print button. Scans the main text for money words. Switches to print mode and checks the print button is hidden. Optionally saves a PDF. Runs an accessibility scan.
inputs: A running app, a database with sample moments, and the EVIDENCE environment variable if a PDF is wanted.
outputs: A pass or fail result. A PDF is written to docs/evidence/F-R-05 only when EVIDENCE is set.
risks: Setting EVIDENCE writes a file into the project. The money-word list is a plain text search, so it can miss money terms written differently.
debug: If the summary count is wrong, check the locked calls and the grading. If the money-word check fails, look for the word in the main text. If the print check fails, check the print styles.
